job: Tell a visitor what the product does, prove it, and send them to sign up.
purpose: The product home of Ember's public site: the call and its result beside the headline, one line of customer logos, the four endpoints with extract as the large cell, cost control beside the usage screen, four checkable figures, one large customer quote and a dark sign-up band above the wordmark footer. Chrome comes from site-shell.js. It has one state: a marketing page has no loading or empty moment.
useWhen: A product needs its public front page, read on a laptop and a phone.
The product can be shown working: a call, a result, a usage screen.

avoidWhen.when: The visitor came to compare plans and prices.
The page tells one customer's story at reading length.
The page is the landing page of the documentation.
The page is the first screen after sign-in.

sections.why: Links follow the brand; the home is the page people arrive on, so the most familiar bar.
A developer believes a call and its result before a claim, so the product sits beside the headline.
Proof as one quiet line under the first screen, not a wall of logos.
One endpoint (extract) is the headline and shows its output; three support it.
The usage screen is the argument for cost control, so it leads and takes the wider column.
Four figures a buyer can check, on one ruled line.
One customer set large, with the way into their story.
The page's one dark band, right before the end.
The home ends on the brand set across the page.

states.name: menu open
states.how: below 900px wide, the header's menu button opens the links as a sheet (data-state="open")
